c201.text: Last time, we left you a dare. Millions of kinds of living things. But scientists sort them into only four groups.

c202.text: Easy! Big ones, small ones, green ones, and scary ones!

c203.text: Hmm. Is Basil right? Did you lock in your four? Let's open the crates and find out.

c301.text: It's You against the Buddies. You lock in first. One finger for every point. And a lizard is hiding. Find it!

c401.text: Look around this farm. A hen. A cat. A tomato plant. A fern. A mushroom. So many living things! How can scientists study them all?

c402.text: Put the ones that are alike together!

c403.text: Yes, Pip! Scientists look for what is the same, and what is different.

c405.text: The grouping of living things based on their similarities and differences is called classification.

h501.text: Are you ready? Three! Two! One! Go!

c601.text: Round one. Scientists classify living things into four main groups. Crate one: plants. Crate two: animals. So where does a mushroom go? One, with the plants. Two, with the animals. Three, in a group of its own. Show me with your fingers.

c603.text: One. It grows from the ground, like a plant.

c604.text: Two! It has no leaves. So it must be an animal!

c605.text: Three. It has no leaves. And it cannot walk.

c606.text: The answer is three. A mushroom is not a plant: it does not make its own food. And it is not an animal. Mushrooms belong to a group called fungi.

c701.text: Three crates are open. Plants. Animals. Fungi. Now, crate four.

c702.text: It's empty! Just a scoop of soil.

c703.text: Look closer, Basil. Much closer. Shrink down. Quietly.

c704.text: You are getting smaller. As small as an ant.

c705.text: Smaller. As small as a grain of sand.

c707.text: Now you can see them. Tiny living things, all around you.

c708.text: Some are shaped like rods. Some are round. Some are spirals.

c709.text: They are too small to see with your eyes alone. But they are living things.

c801.text: Crate four is not empty. These tiny living things are bacteria.

c802.text: Bacteria are tiny living things and they come in different shapes and sizes.

c805.text: Living things can be classified into four main groups: plants, animals, fungi and bacteria.

c806.text: So not big, small, green and scary?

c807.text: No, Basil. Size and colour do not decide the group.

c902.text: Plants are living things that usually have leaves, stems and roots. They are able to make their own food when there is light.

c903.text: Animals are unable to make their own food. They depend on other living things for food.

c1001.text: My rule. If it is green, it is a plant. A tomato plant: green. A fern: green. A grasshopper: green!

c1002.text: Something is not right. If you can spot it, cross your arms. Hold on!

c1003.text: Arms crossed? One finger up! A grasshopper is green. But it is an animal. It is unable to make its own food. It eats leaves.

c1004.text: So colour is not the clue! I will ask: can it make its own food?

c1201.text: Show me your score hand! More than one? You beat the Buddies. Two fingers? High five!

c1202.text: Did you spot the lizard? It was on the water pipe. Which crate does a lizard go in? Tell someone at home.

h860.text: Let's read today's key words together! Ready?

c1301.text: The plants crate is full. But scientists sort plants again, into two groups.

c1302.text: Look! This chilli plant has no flowers today. Not one!

c1303.text: No flowers today. So is it a flowering plant? Find out in Part Two!
